thesis: Tonight's close carries a risk premium for two inflation prints, not one. When CPI and PPI land on consecutive sessions the market prices the pair as a single block, and the duration holder gets paid to sit through the second, lower-information half of it: the PPI session pays TLT +25.8 bps when a CPI printed on its eve against +8.4 bps when one did not, and the session immediately before the print pays nothing at all. The other side is whoever bought protection across the block and unwinds it once the headline number is out, plus the rates shorts positioned for a producer print that almost never moves the story after CPI has. Consensus treats PPI as a footnote, which is the reason the premium survives to be collected. 95% of the payoff arrives in the 08:30 gap, so this is a one-session release trade and nothing else.
